title: Now in the Heat of Youthful Blood
description: Now in the Heat of Youthful Blood in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 91, headed “Advice to youth; or, Old age and death in an unconverted state, Eccles. 12. 1 7. Isa. 65. 20”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Now in the heat of youth-ful blood Re-mem-ber your Cre-a-tor God, Be-hold the months come has-tening on When you shall say, "My joys are gone."

lines: Now in the heat of youthful blood
Behold the months come hastening on
When you shall say, "My joys are gone."
Laden with guilt and heavy woes
Down to the regions of the dead,
With endless curses on his head.
The dust returns to dust again,
The soul in agonies of pain
Ascends to God, not there to dwell,
But hears her doom, and sinks to hell.
Eternal King! I fear thy Name,
Teach me to know how frail I am;
And when my soul must hence remove,
Give me a mansion in thy love.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
